title: Battle of White Mountain
summary: On 8 November 1620 an imperial and Catholic force under Emperor Ferdinand II defeated the army of the Bohemian Estates on the White Mountain (Bílá Hora), west of Prague. The fighting lasted about two hours. Twenty-seven rebel leaders were later executed and the Estates lost their power.

uncertainty.note: A Royal Collection print heading cites an older catalogue listing 7 November 1620; the catalogue text itself gives 8 November.

where.modern_name: Bílá Hora, near Prague, Czech Republic
where.historical_name: White Mountain, near Prague, Kingdom of Bohemia (Habsburg lands)

importance.justification: Decisive defeat of the Bohemian Revolt, early in the Thirty Years' War, that ended Bohemian Estates' power.
